relations: If amber liquid seeps at the base, it wets nearby granules while farther grains stay dry.
As the wet band spreads, the dome's crisp lower edge softens into a more diffuse contour.
When the wet surface deforms, specular highlights drift, stretch, and split without moving the dome body.
The orange dome stays centered and broadly constant in size while its base liquid halo widens.
caption: An extreme close-up holds a glossy, translucent orange dome resting on a bed of fine white granules, its wet surface catching a pale crescent highlight near the top and a small bright blob on the right. A fringe of granules already clings to the dome's lower rim. Over the sequence a thin amber liquid seeps out at the base and spreads laterally into the surrounding granules, darkening and wetting that band while the grains farther out stay dry and white. The crisp wavy edge of the dome's bottom softens into a smoother, more diffuse contour as the liquid halo widens. The specular highlights slowly reshape and drift, the right-side blob stretching into a streak and then splitting, consistent with a deforming wet surface. A faint pale squiggle on the left shifts slightly in form. The dome stays centered and broadly constant in size, so the dominant change is the spreading liquid and reshaping reflections rather than any large movement of the body.
